text:
Maya: quick heads-up — prod token/sec dropped ~18% since Friday's merge (r3456). Seeing lots of tiny batches and queueing delays. Starting a lightweight profile now.
Liam: did alerts pick this up? any CI perf failures? cc @deploy-bot
deploy-bot: CI perf job 'throughput/regression' flagged a 20% drop on xlarge-runner. https://ci.internal/reports/1796 (summary attached)
Maya: CI flagged it but the rollout continued. local bisect points at commit a1b2c3 — 'pipepack: reduce coalescing window, new allocator path'.
Sophia: that change touched the coalescer heuristics + allocator fast-path. My hunch: more undersized batches -> kernel selection falls back to scalar path. Pulling flamegraphs now.
Ash: I can reproduce on my laptop with the smoke harness: `./bench/pipeline --model=llama-13b --seq=1024 --concurrency=4`. Before: 1450 tok/s, after: 1180 tok/s.
Maya: flamegraph snippet I uploaded:
```text
coalescer.c      42%  (pipepack coalesce loop)
kernel_dispatch.cpp 28%  (dispatch -> scalar_matmul slowpath)
kv_cache.cpp     10%
other            20%
```
Liam: sounds like two factors: coalescer threshold change + allocator fragmentation creating more small batches. New kernel pick logic picks slower kernels for batch_size < 16. Suggest revert the window change to 32 and re-run tests.
Sophia: alternative: force kernel fallback to the optimized avx2/packed kernel for small batches in the short term, and add a metric for `backend_choice` + batch_size histogram. That will prove causality.
Maya: I'll open a hotfix PR to bump coalescing window and add the metric. @Ash can you run a canary in eu-west-1 with synthetic traffic?
Ash: starting canary now:
```
scripts/deploy_canary --region=eu-west-1 --tag=hotfix/pipepack-coalesce
```
deploy-bot: Canary deployment started: canary-1796018420-hotfix
Ash: tailing canary logs — batch_size histogram is shifting from mode=4 -> mode=16 within ~10m, token/sec recovered to +10% vs baseline. Initial KV hitrate unchanged.
Liam: if canary numbers hold, we should revert a1b2c3 and then reapply allocator changes in smaller PRs (split coalescer refactor + allocator change). Also add a unit test that asserts kernel selection for batch sizes 1..32 picks the expected fast path.
Maya: filed issue PLTF-987 and PR draft: https://git.internal/redwood/pull/1234 — contains window bump + metrics + a one-line safeguard in kernel_dispatch to prefer gep-packed kernels for small but frequent batches. Will push tests shortly.
Sophia: also adding an e2e perf test to CI that simulates the small-batch distribution so this doesn't slip through.
Ash: canary looks stable for 30m. I'll keep it running and then roll the hotfix forward after +60m. :thumbsup:
Maya: thanks team. Keeping rollout on hold until PR merges and canary proves out.
